# Good practices and traps

Where a diagnostic or a source file covers an item, it is named in brackets.

**Qualities and gates**

1. **Latching enums never list "undecided".** The first read latches the placeholder and the arc never starts. Leave the unset state as no value and write the rubric to stay silent until it happens. (Diagnostic `latching-enum-placeholder`.)
2. **Gate only on what the extraction pass can observe.** Thoughts, off-screen events and things the narrator never writes leave the gate shut and the story stalled.
3. **Make the rubric and the exit's `extraction_hint` say the same thing**, in the fiction's own words, never a name the player has not heard yet.
4. **Party moves are `evidence_from: "party"`, outcomes that open an anchor are `world`.** Under `world` a party move is never proved by the player's line; under `any` an outcome is proved by the player writing that it happened. (Diagnostic `quality-outcome-player-evidence`.)
5. **Calibrate `commit_evidence` with real accept and hold lines**, and avoid bare words.
6. **Chance rolls only on code-sourced bool or int qualities**, and a roll decides the world, never the player's act. (Parser `readRoll`.)
7. **Name each clue as its own value** rather than gating on a loose counter.
8. **Give a `location` enum player labels and list the places under scene read.** (Diagnostic `scene-read-location-empty`.)

**Cast and speakers**

9. **Requirements name characters by card name, never roster id.** (Diagnostic `requirement-member-roster-id`.)
10. **First messages for the opening scene only; `cast_changes` mutes later arrivals at the start beat** and enables each where they enter. (Rule text in `src/copilot/prompts.ts`.)
11. **A talk lead goes in `speakers`, and so does every enabled character the player may address.** (Diagnostic `talk-lead-outside-speakers`.)
12. **Use `{{groupNotMuted}}` on a narrator card, not `{{group}}`.** `{{group}}` includes muted members and the narrator treats them as present.
13. **Give every character the narrator must recognise a lore or scene line.** A muted character with no lore gets recast as whatever the narrator guesses, such as a "royal advisor".
14. **Card names are first names.** "X the Y" makes every "the" a mention of that member.

**Steering text**

15. **Drives and motives are the character's private aim, in one line, never a plan for the player and never for the player's persona.** (Diagnostics `motive-for-player`, `motive-member-unknown`.)
16. **Guidance is pressure and intent, never the ending, and a secret goes in the member's own entry.**
17. **Call the player `{{user}}`, never "the player".**
18. **One house rule, one demand.** (Diagnostic `house-rule-compound`.)
19. **Set or clear the author's note on purpose.** A beat without one keeps the last; a beat with one loses its objective line. (Diagnostic `checkpoint-inherits-author-note`; `engine/agency.ts`.)
20. **Choose `objective_kind` per beat, and give refusals an `alternate` that rejoins.** (`engine/agency.ts`.)

**Scripted lines and openers**

21. **Scripted lines have no time or place check.** Word them to fit wherever they fire, or use an `llm` reply with an instruction.
22. **Exactly one scripted `new_chat_only` opener per story, plus at most one opening hook** (an `llm` `new_chat_only` reply, usually `ask_player`), and no scripted opener when an entering reply already introduces the character.

**Lore**

23. **The World Info curator creates only what play established twice.** A new entry needs two live facts naming it and the author's accept; seed its book with every entry play should keep current. (`src/stagecraft/createPlan.ts`.)
24. **Checkpoint-gated lore and curator scope never overlap.** Gated entries are rebuilt from the path each beat, so the curator is refused there. (`stagecraft/scope.ts`.)
25. **A gated secret is never a constant entry with no character filter.**
26. **Every book the story relies on is under `requirements.lorebooks`**: beat lore, lore select and the curator book. (Diagnostic `lore-select-inactive`.)
27. **Check lore keys against the whole cast.** A place keyed "Venn" fires every time Mara Venn is named.

**Player copy**

28. **`player_name`, `player_text` and chapter `player_title` show to the player**: name the place, not the outcome, and keep them true on every path in.
